ai.description: This 20–30 cm snake features a dark brown body with a prominent, continuous red mid-dorsal stripe. It has a small, pointed head and a truncated, shield-like tail characteristic of the Uropeltidae family.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis rubrolineata* is best identified by the distinct, continuous reddish-orange stripe running along the center of its back, which contrasts with the dark body.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis rubrolineata* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Red-lined Earth Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis rubrolineata* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis rubrolineata* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
